taken.mechanism: EV-02: Activation is the union of dedicated skill-tool calls and plain reads of <name>/SKILL.md at a path boundary. None means unobservable; an empty list means offered, none chosen.
EV-03: Install-and-discover only: skills sit in the agent's native skills root and are never preloaded or pasted. A copy in the working directory is a back-door that makes activation unfalsifiable.

EV-03: Closed neighbourhood: only declared skills are installed, so the observed activation set is a subset of the declared list and exact-set assertions are affordable. Delegation chains are enumerated, not inferred.

EV-09: Attempt outcomes are typed (pass, task_fail, judge_error, infra_error, timeout, cheat, not_checked), not a pass bool. Unusable outcomes leave the denominator and are reported as a separate unusable count.

EV-09: Outcomes are classified at one seam with a fixed precedence (setup failed, cancelled, timeout, infra error, cheat, not checked, judge). Signals travel structurally, never by sniffing strings in error text.
EV-11: A zero-exit attempt with no model call observed is infra_error, not a verdict: judging it scored an expired login as a real 0% and let an empty activation probe pass.
EV-12: An errored grader is dropped, not failed: the surviving check's verdict stands, and a hung assertion has no verdict rather than task_fail. judge_error fires only when no verdict survives.
EV-14: Raw single-run success rate is the headline, not pass@k, which flatters flaky skills: one pass in three reads as 70.4%. pass@k and pass^k stay as secondary views.
EV-15: No early stop on non-activation: a miss is usable data; truncating after N misses biases weak descriptions down (a true 20% rate reads 0% a third of the time).
EV-32: An attempt is not a security boundary: isolation only keeps measurement clean. Symlink targets are screened against exclusions so hint.md -> answers/key.md cannot smuggle an answer key.

EV-16: Seven separate decision dimensions (compatibility, completeness, assurance, golden, billing, statistics, operations), each with its own nonpass states. Aggregation keeps the strongest state, so a golden failure cannot become 'missing'.
EV-16: Golden tasks must pass first attempt in both arms for every planned trial; retries cannot erase a golden failure, and golden or operational errors stay out of averages.
EV-17: Never drop missing samples or change their denominator: omitted cluster or task mass is rejected, not repaired, and missing publication cannot become merely partial.
EV-20: Independence must be justified before a strict pass: fresh workspaces, sessions or set order do not establish it, since shared service, time or state can break it. Otherwise inconclusive.

GS-53: Adversarial packs as golden tasks: injection arrives via fixture files (ticket, README) and scope-bypass asks for out-of-scope actions. Tasks list forbidden tools and strings; unsafe outcomes fail the gate.

HD-61: Durable collection journal: new private directory, files synced before engines start, each attempt start synced before the request, one terminal per attempt. Interrupted runs are never repaired or resumed.

taken.mechanism: EV-02: Host-agnostic activation check: the skill counts as engaged if the run shows a Skill tool call (namespace stripped) or a command reading the skill's files. With no telemetry it errors.

EV-13: Pricing coverage is checked before the first task dispatches; unpriced models warn and totals become floors, since missing cost is recoverable from tokens and a lost run is not.
EV-15: Early stop is one-sided: a pass-stop ends the run once positives are decided, so later misfires are never seen. Precision and recall must come from the full-run variant.

EV-32: A leak detector needs a positive control: the check that the agent's view holds no grading material is paired with a planted sentinel, so 'staged nothing' cannot pass vacuously.
